summary: This Dockerfile sets up a development container for a Docusaurus blog project with Node.js. It starts from a custom base image, installs essential tools and Git, configures passwordless sudo for the node user, sets up VSCode server integration for remote development, customizes the bash shell with history and a styled prompt, and installs project dependencies using Yarn with caching for faster rebuilds.

explanations.1: This special comment tells Docker to use version 1.6 of the Dockerfile syntax, which includes modern features like cache mounts that make rebuilds faster.
explanations.8: ARG creates a build-time variable that can be passed in when building the image; this one sets the user ID to 1002, which will be used later to create a non-root user.
explanations.16: This pulls a pre-built image called 'blog-docusaurus' that already has Node.js and Docusaurus dependencies installed, saving time instead of installing everything from scratch.
explanations.19: We re-declare APP_HOME here because build arguments don't automatically carry over between stages, so we need to remind Docker what APP_HOME should be for the rest of this Dockerfile.
explanations.25: The --mount flags tell Docker to cache the apt package lists and cache directories, so if you rebuild the image, it won't re-download packages you already have.
explanations.27: The 'set -eux' command makes bash exit on errors, print each command before running it, and treat undefined variables as errors—all safety measures to catch problems early.
explanations.38: This tells Git to trust the application directory, preventing warnings when running Git commands inside the container later.
explanations.48: We're writing a sudoers configuration file that lets the node user run any command with sudo without needing to enter a password.
explanations.49: The chmod 0440 sets very restrictive permissions on the sudoers file—this is a security requirement, as sudoers files must have specific permissions or sudo will refuse to read them.
explanations.53: We're creating directories where VSCode's remote server extension will store its files, extensions, and metadata for remote development.
explanations.60: We're appending configuration to .bashrc so that bash history gets saved to a file, making command history persistent across container restarts.
explanations.67: This customizes the bash prompt to show a Docker whale emoji, the current username, and working directory in a colored format for better readability during development.
explanations.71: We're setting an environment variable that tells Yarn where to cache downloaded packages, so future yarn installs can reuse those files instead of re-downloading.
explanations.79: The --mount flag with uid and gid parameters mounts the Yarn cache folder with the correct ownership, so the node user can read and write to it without permission issues.
explanations.81: The --immutable and --frozen-lockfile flags ensure we install exact versions from the lock file; --prefer-offline uses cached packages when possible to speed things up.
explanations.82: We're installing Sharp, a native image processing library that Docusaurus needs to optimize images; the platform and arch flags ensure we get the Linux 64-bit version.
